title: Why Is the Bottom of Every Ship Painted Red?

scenes.text: Pull any ship out of the water, and the bottom is always the same colour.
Never blue. Never green. Red, on almost every hull in the world.
It looks like tradition, or a rule nobody ever questioned.
But that colour is a side effect of keeping the ship alive.
Below the waterline, barnacles and weed grow on bare steel within weeks.
A fouled hull drags through the water, and drag burns fuel.
So the paint is loaded with copper compounds that stop anything from taking hold.
Copper oxide is naturally red, and cheap enough to cover a hull the size of a building.
The colour was never a choice. It is simply what protection looks like.
